cfg_battery_section_charging_hint: Charging performance and an optional 80% limit with a custom local-time interval.
nc_state_invalid_window: invalid interval: start and end must differ
t_nc_off: Night charge limit off · ASB restriction released
wb_handover: Mobile data stays ready while the screen is on, which uses a little more battery

night_charge_enable.name: Night Charge Limit
night_charge_enable.desc: Optional charging control for a custom interval. While charging inside the window, ASB uses a supported standard kernel control to hold around 80%; at the end it restores the exact previous value. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; windows may cross midnight, but equal endpoints are invalid. It never discharges a battery above 80%, does not replace OEM Adaptive Charging and is off by default. If no writable control exists, the status says not exposed. Disable, window exit or uninstall restores only values still owned by ASB.

night_charge_start.name: Charge window start
night_charge_start.desc: Local time when the optional 80% window begins. Start is inclusive; changing it reconciles charging immediately.

night_charge_end.name: Charge window end
night_charge_end.desc: Local time when ASB restores the previous kernel value. End is exclusive and must differ from start; an earlier end crosses midnight.

net_mtu_probing.name: TCP MTU Recovery
net_mtu_probing.desc: For mobile or VPN routes where blocked path MTU discovery makes connections stall. On enables the kernel probe only after a suspected black hole; healthy routes keep their normal MSS. This is not a general speed boost. Stock and uninstall restore the exact previous 0, 1 or 2 value.

athena_service.name: Athena Background Killer
athena_service.desc: Controls OxygenOS's AthenaService background-app killer. Off disables only that component while leaving the rest of com.oplus.athena in place; this may help apps that the OEM kills despite Android battery exemptions. More apps remaining active can increase RAM use and background drain, and notification behaviour still depends on each app. Stock restores the component state recorded by ASB; uninstall also restores it.

descOpt.stock: OxygenOS keeps its normal Athena background policy.
descOpt.off: Disable only AthenaService. Apps may stay active longer, with more RAM use and background drain.

heytap_mcs.name: HeyTap MCS / OPPO Push
heytap_mcs.desc: Off disables com.heytap.mcs without replacing system files. Apps using HeyTap/OPPO Push can stop receiving notifications or receive them late. Enabling also requests one profile-guided ART compilation after the next reboot; it can temporarily use CPU, storage and battery. Stock restores the MCS state ASB changed and cancels a compilation that has not started. After the reboot it waits for the charger (Charging or Full), so the compilation does not heat or drain a phone in your hand; with no charger within 24 h it stays pending until the next boot.

descOpt.stock: Leave MCS under Android/OEM control and cancel a compilation request that has not started.
descOpt.off: Disable HeyTap push transport and request one ART compilation after the next reboot. Check affected app notifications.

documentsui_fix.name: DocumentsUI / DSU Picker Fix
documentsui_fix.desc: One-time repair for the system file picker on affected ColorOS/DSU setups. Enables and unhides DocumentsUI, resets its picker/files activities, and disables ColorOS File Manager for user 0. The File Manager returns on Off. Only states ASB changed are restored; nothing is re-applied at boot.

descOpt.stock: Keep the ROM's Doze timing; remove the ASB override.
descOpt.night: Apply earlier Doze only during the learned sleep window.
descOpt.moderate: Target idle entry after five minutes with the screen off.
descOpt.aggressive: Target idle entry after two minutes and shorten selected sensing/location windows. Background work may be deferred.

doze_level.desc: Controls how quickly Android enters Doze after the screen turns off. Stock keeps the ROM timing; Moderate targets five minutes and Aggressive two minutes, while Night applies only in the learned sleep window. Doze can defer background network, jobs and alarms until maintenance windows; high-priority push may still arrive. Use Stock if timely background activity matters more than earlier idle entry. Stock removes the ASB timing override.

descOpt.off: Leave every managed Google component in its recorded original state.
descOpt.safe: Disable selected telemetry and reporting components. Check apps that depend on them.
descOpt.more: Also disable selected advertising and measurement components. Reversible, but dependent features may change.

gms_freeze.desc: Disables individual Google Play services components. Levels are cumulative. SAFE: telemetry, stats and analytics - nothing the phone needs. MORE: adds the ad identifier, location reporting and the backup scheduler. MAX: adds Icing indexing and background Fitness recording. THE COST OF MAX: in-app and system search will miss some results, and steps are not counted in the background. Push notifications are untouched at every level. Everything is restored by switching to off - each component's original state is recorded.

descOpt.stock: Leave Play services background scheduling under ROM control.
descOpt.lite: Limit selected location and search-widget background work.
descOpt.strict: Also remove the Play services Doze exemption; push and sync may be delayed.

gms_trim.desc: Reduces selected Google Play services background activity without disabling Play services itself. Lite limits location reporting and search-widget background work. Strict also removes Play services from the Doze exemption list, which can delay push notifications, sync and other background jobs. Choose Lite or Stock if timely delivery is essential. Changed permissions and exemptions are recorded and restored when ASB is removed.

descOpt.stock: Leave the current phantom-process setting untouched.
descOpt.relaxed: Disable the limit. Background child processes can survive, but runaway resource use is less contained.
descOpt.strict: Explicitly set Android's limit to 32 phantom processes.

phantom_procs.desc: Controls Android's limit on app-created phantom processes outside the normal activity lifecycle. No Limit disables that protection so long terminal jobs, emulators and compiles can survive, but runaway apps can also consume more memory and CPU. Limit 32 explicitly restores Android's ceiling. Leave Alone preserves the current device value, which another tool may have changed. Restart the affected app because the limit is read when its process starts.

descOpt.0: Minimise device and ASB diagnostics. Later bug reports may lack the evidence needed for analysis.
descOpt.2: Add learner updates and screen transitions; useful for battery investigations.
descOpt.3: Verbose diagnostics that grow quickly. Use only while reproducing a problem.
descOpt.stock: Do not change device logging through this setting.

log_level.desc: Controls ASB log detail and, except in Stock, selected device logging. Stock leaves device logging untouched. 0 minimises device and module diagnostics, making later bug reports much less useful. 1 records normal significant events; 2 adds learner and screen-transition details useful for battery reports; 3 is verbose and grows quickly, so use it only while reproducing a problem. Returning from 0 restores the logging state recorded by ASB.

descOpt.stock: Use the device trip point read from its CPU thermal zone at boot.
descOpt.smart: Start from that point and allow bounded upward adjustment after qualifying sustained sessions.
descOpt.manual: Use the temperature selected below without Smart adjustment.

descOpt.auto: Do not change the system's current effect level.
descOpt.stock: Use the device's normal effects and Recents presentation.
descOpt.flat: Simplify effects. Recents becomes a plain list and OxygenOS hides the Cards/Simple selector; OnePlus 15 only.

ui_effects_level.desc: Normal keeps the device's full transition and Recents effects. Simplified reduces visual effects and may lower GPU use, but Recents becomes a plain list and OxygenOS removes the Cards/Simple selector. Restore Normal and reboot to recover it. The simplified option is exposed only on the OnePlus 15 because its behaviour on other models has not been validated.

descOpt.auto: Choose an initial route window from measured link conditions.
descOpt.off: Restore the route values recorded before ASB changed them.
descOpt.aggressive: Use a larger window; poor links may see more retransmissions.

net_route_tune.desc: Adjusts the initial TCP burst size for routes. Smart chooses from measured link conditions and leaves weak links closer to the factory value; Moderate is conservative, while Aggressive selects a larger class and can increase retransmissions on poor links. Stock restores the previous route values. This changes connection ramp-up, not the maximum speed of the radio or service.

descOpt.auto: Leave the ROM's Bluetooth audio path unchanged.
descOpt.on: Request hardware/offloaded encoding where supported. Actual power use depends on the device and codec.
descOpt.off: Use CPU encoding. This can let some equaliser apps process Bluetooth audio, with potentially higher CPU use.

net_rps.name: Spread Network Load
net_rps.desc: Chooses which CPU cores may receive packets for Wi-Fi interfaces. Stock leaves the kernel and driver configuration untouched. Little uses the efficiency cluster; All allows every core. Spreading work can help on fast links but wakes more CPUs and may cost power on light traffic. Mobile-data receive distribution is left to the device. Actual gains depend on the driver and link.

descOpt.stock: Leave the kernel and driver receive-packet masks untouched.
descOpt.little: Allow receive processing on the efficiency cluster.
descOpt.all: Allow receive processing on every CPU cluster; more cores may wake.

net_txqueue.name: Transmit Queue
net_txqueue.desc: Sets how many packets may wait in the Wi-Fi transmit queue. Stock keeps the driver value; Short uses 256 and Shorter uses 128. Smaller queues can reduce delay under load, but may limit throughput or increase loss on fast or variable links. If uploads, streaming or latency become worse, return to Stock.

descOpt.short: Use 256 packets. Can reduce queued delay but may not suit every fast link.
descOpt.shorter: Use 128 packets. Test throughput, loss and latency under load.

night_modem_idle.name: Quiet Radio at Night
night_modem_idle.desc: During the learned sleep window, extends cellular keepalive intervals and gates selected rmnet data-path wakeups so the modem path can stay idle longer. Push notifications and app sync may wait until a later wake. Calls and SMS use separate modem paths; ASB does not change radio power, airplane mode, roaming or network selection. Changes are recorded and restored when disabled or uninstalled.

gnss_trim.name: Trim Background GPS
gnss_trim.desc: Limits background location use by eligible user-installed apps whose processes are cached while the screen is off. Such apps are reduced to coarse location and regain normal precision when opened. Navigation, fitness/route tracking, emergency, find-my and foreground apps are excluded. This can reduce location-related wakeups, but background features in an affected app may lose precise tracks or geofence accuracy.

smart_media_guard.name: Smart Media Guard
smart_media_guard.desc: Optional, Smart-only protection for a narrow case: a known video, feed or browser app stays game-like CPU + GPU heavy for a full minute while you use it on battery. ASB then keeps only the effective GPU ceiling at the existing 70% media envelope. It never limits a known game, an unknown app, charging, thermal protection, CPU ceilings or frequency floors. Start with the 12-hour trial; turn it off if a high-refresh stream stutters.

radio_policy_enable.name: Cellular / radio controls
radio_policy_enable.desc: Independent master for ASB modem controls. OFF is the default: choosing any power profile leaves Android’s mobile-data context and TCP keepalive settings untouched. This is the recommended setting on WiFi-only or no-SIM devices. Turn it on only if this phone uses a SIM/eSIM and you deliberately want ASB’s separate radio options below. Turning it off immediately restores the Android values recorded before ASB changed them; it never changes airplane mode, carrier selection, roaming, preferred network type, Bluetooth or audio.

bt_link_stability.name: Bluetooth Link Stability
bt_link_stability.desc: Optional workaround for Bluetooth audio dropouts during playback. Stable suppresses Wi-Fi scanning while audio plays, which can help on devices where the two radios interfere. New networks may appear more slowly. No codec is forced and pairing is unchanged. Leave this off if your connection is already stable.

BG_TRIM_LEVEL.desc: Controls how strongly ASB restricts background apps. Off leaves Android in charge and restores buckets changed by ASB. Safe adjusts standby buckets for apps that Android reports as unused, with critical apps protected. Aggressive adds stronger background and memory limits; apps may wake less often, lose state or deliver notifications late. Disruptive package or vendor-service actions require a separate explicit opt-in and are not enabled by this level alone.

mglru_hold.name: Keep Apps In Memory
mglru_hold.desc: Protects the working set from reclaim so the foreground app is not evicted under memory pressure and rebuilt when you return to it. HOLD: 1 second of protection. AGGRESSIVE: 2 seconds - apps survive longer, less free RAM. Only has an effect on kernels with MGLRU; elsewhere the tweak does nothing.

net_wifi_leave.name: Leave Bad Wi-Fi
net_wifi_leave.desc: Helps move away from a connected Wi-Fi network that has a weak signal or carries no usable traffic. Higher levels act sooner. With the screen on, ASB turns Wi-Fi off briefly and back on; repeated failures lengthen the pause from 30 seconds up to five minutes. This can interrupt active Wi-Fi sessions and may cause mobile-data use. It works independently of Cellular controls.

descOpt.off: Do not actively leave Wi-Fi; Android and the driver control handover.
descOpt.weak: Act when signal falls below −80 dBm.
descOpt.unusable: Also act when a connected link carries no usable traffic.
descOpt.aggressive: Use the fastest handover rules; Wi-Fi interruptions and mobile-data use are more likely.

descOpt.0: Suppress ASB-managed background scans; manual scans can still be initiated by the system or user.
descOpt.1: Allow a background scan about every 10 minutes.
descOpt.2: Allow a background scan about every 5 minutes.
descOpt.3: Allow a background scan about every 2 minutes.
descOpt.5: Allow a background scan about every 30 minutes; discovery can be much slower.

wifi_scan_throttle.desc: Controls how often ASB allows background Wi-Fi scanning. Less frequent scanning can reduce radio activity when you stay in one place, but known and new networks may be discovered later. This does not change the active connection's data rate. Choose Unthrottled to leave scanning unrestricted; the option descriptions below show each interval.

wifi_powersave.name: WiFi Power Save

descOpt.off: Keep the Wi-Fi radio awake between packets.
descOpt.screen_off: Enable Wi-Fi power saving only while the display is off.
descOpt.always: Keep Wi-Fi power saving enabled during use and with the screen off.

wifi_powersave.desc: Controls Wi-Fi power saving between packets. Screen Off enables it only while the display is off; Always also enables it during use. Lower radio activity can reduce power use but may add latency or affect games, casting and Wi-Fi calls. Off keeps the radio fully awake. Actual behaviour and savings depend on the driver and access point.

ltpo_force.name: Force LTPO Refresh
ltpo_force.desc:
Applies a patch prepared from the device's own oplus_vrr_config.json: it enables supported panel power-saving paths left off by the OEM and disables selected display telemetry. The stock file is not modified. If no suitable table or change is found, the switch does nothing and the status badge explains why. Applying the table requires a reboot.

The Android refresh range is also opened: ASB removes its floor, uses the highest reported panel mode, restores the maximum on touch and selects 60 Hz after two quiet seconds so panel adaptation can continue. Camera, game and video ownership are preserved, and previous range values are restored on handback. If the verified OnePlus15-165HZ-LTPO writer is present, ASB yields unless you explicitly give ASB priority. A same-target bind from another module always keeps ownership: ASB neither stacks over it nor removes it. Power savings and low-idle rates depend on the panel and ROM; neither is guaranteed.

mmfeed_off.name: Multimedia Telemetry Off
mmfeed_off.desc: Uses the device's own Multimedia_Feedback_List.xml to disable the multimedia feedback collector's isOpen switch, then binds the patched copy over the stock path without modifying the original file. The patch is prepared during installation and applied only when this switch is on; a reboot is required. If the file is absent or already closed, the switch does nothing and the badge reports that state. This can reduce diagnostic logging and I/O, but battery savings are not guaranteed. Audio and video processing are not changed.

net_screen_off_lte.name: LTE While Screen Off
net_screen_off_lte.desc: After the screen has been off for 90 seconds, prefers LTE instead of keeping 5G NSA active; the previous setting returns when the screen turns on. Calls and sufficiently heavy transfers are excluded, and a recent transfer can keep 5G for at least 10 minutes. Off by default because changing allowed network types can briefly re-register mobile data. If the ROM rejects the change, ASB restores the previous value and stops retrying.

net_lte_light.name: 5G Only When Needed
net_lte_light.desc: With the screen on, switches from 5G NSA to LTE after three minutes of light mobile traffic below 2 Mbit/s. Sustained traffic above the implemented thresholds restores 5G and holds it for 10 minutes. ASB does not switch during calls, tethering, games or Wi-Fi use. Off by default: every network-type change can briefly re-register mobile data, and actual power use depends on the modem and signal.

descOpt.keep: Leave LSPosed settings and logs under LSPosed's control.
descOpt.off: Disable LSPosed verbose logging from its next start, remove old verbose logs and periodically clear the Modules log.

lsposed_verbose.desc: Keep leaves LSPosed settings and logs under LSPosed's control. Off changes LSPosed's own Verbose log setting, removes old verbose-log files and takes effect after LSPosed restarts or the phone reboots. The modules log - what the LSPosed modules themselves write - has no switch in LSPosed, so while Off is selected ASB also clears it periodically. This can remove evidence needed to debug another module. If you later enable verbose logging in LSPosed, ASB does not reverse that choice; Keep restores ownership without secretly managing LSPosed.

kernel_sched_stats.name: Scheduler Debug Accounting
kernel_sched_stats.desc: Opt-in generic kernel tweak. Off disables scheduler debug statistics only when /proc/sys/kernel/sched_stats is exposed and writable. Scheduling policy, CPU frequencies and SoC drivers are untouched. Stock and uninstall restore the exact original 0/1. No unmeasured battery percentage is claimed.

descOpt.off: Disable only an exposed writable sched_stats node; restore its recorded value on Stock or uninstall.

zygisk_enabled.name: ASB Zygisk
zygisk_enabled.desc: Master switch for attaching ASB to Zygisk in newly started app processes, or leaving them unattached after their next restart. Off preserves the selected mode, automatic app list, feature switches, guard and ART settings; enabling again restores that saved setup without silently choosing a new preset. The full control panel is on the ZYGISK page. Requires a Zygisk-capable root implementation. Safe mode and a broker failure fail open; existing apps are not killed.

zygisk_hints.name: Zygisk Lifecycle Refresh
zygisk_hints.desc: An accepted start/exit from the observer allowlist asks the existing governor for fresh evidence while the screen is on. At most 8 requests/minute, at least 2 seconds apart. Zygisk chooses no frequency, profile or app policy; thermal, dwell and vendor limits remain authoritative. Acknowledgement is not a boost or proof of power saving. LSPosed is never killed, hidden, frozen or throttled. The rate limit applies per active companion.

zygisk_launch.name: Zygisk Cold-Start Lift
zygisk_launch.desc: When zygote starts a new process for the app you are opening (Android marks it as the top app), ASB hears it at once and covers the launch with the unlock lift: a running lift is carried over the start, otherwise one is armed even inside the 5-second anti-chatter gap. No package name is sent; profile, thermal, warm-die and lift-length rules still decide. At most one cold start per second and 20 per minute; costs one short companion connection per cold start. Needs the Zygisk Process Observer switch, not the allowlist. Faster cold starts are expected, not proven: compare `am start -W` times with this on and off.

zygisk_ledger.name: Zygisk Process-Start Ledger
zygisk_ledger.desc: Counts, for this boot, how many processes each ordinary app starts with the screen off and on. Apps that keep starting work at night are a common hidden battery drain; the top ones appear in Device diagnostics and asbdiag. Package names and counts only, kept in memory (tmpfs); nothing is restricted automatically. Costs one short companion connection per app process start while on. Needs the Zygisk Process Observer switch.

dsp_outputs.desc: Choose which outputs ASB DSP may process: the built-in speaker, wired headphones/USB DACs, or Bluetooth. Unavailable outputs are ignored. Off bypasses the whole DSP while preserving every level for later. Bluetooth processing can move playback away from hardware offload and increase screen-off CPU use; exclude Bluetooth if long listening sessions matter more than the effect.

dsp_loudness.desc: ASB DSP adds up to +25 dB of gain, with optional compression and a final sample-peak limiter. Start at +3 dB: high settings can sound heavily compressed even when peaks are limited. The first enable needs a reboot. DSP is bypassed in the external-EQ audio profile. On the speaker, gain is reduced when the battery reaches 42 °C and restored below 40 °C; wired and Bluetooth gains are not reduced by this rule.

dsp_voice.desc: Requires DSP Loudness. Two broad bands adjust voice body at 350 Hz and upper-edge sharpness at 3 kHz. Level 10 applies +5 dB and −6 dB respectively. This can make thin or harsh speech fuller, especially on the phone speaker; high values may sound unnatural. Start at 4–6 and use DSP Outputs to limit the effect to the outputs that need it. Changes apply live before the limiter.

audio_remove_volume_limit.desc: Removes Android's headphone volume ceiling so the existing slider can go higher; it does not add gain by itself. Off by default. This reduces a safety boundary, not just a warning: sustained loud listening can cause permanent hearing damage. Use the lowest comfortable level and limit listening time. Reboot if your ROM reads the policy only at startup.

audio_resampler.desc: Controls the quality of Android's sample-rate conversion when the source and output rates differ. Stock leaves the ROM unchanged; High and Max use longer, steeper filters, with Max costing the most CPU. Any audible difference depends on the recording and equipment and may be negligible. Playback already at the output rate, hardware-offloaded playback and Bluetooth codec encoding are not changed. Reboot to apply.

media_vol_steps.desc: Changes the number of media-volume positions without raising the maximum volume. More steps give finer control, especially at low listening levels. Stock keeps the ROM value; 20–100 selects a fixed count in steps of five. Reboot to apply. The saved slider position may then map to a quieter level, so check it once. Some ROMs ignore this setting; the action button and asbdiag report the value actually in use.

CAMERA_LEVEL.desc: Scales the firmware's own photo/video colour, detail and sharpening values. 0 keeps stock tuning; 1–6 increase processing gradually, while 7–10 are deliberately strong and stylised. Device capability limits still apply. Level 10 targets up to 2.5× chroma, 3.4× AI blend and 3.5× sharpness before those clamps. Reboot to rebuild from the stock baseline. High levels can exaggerate noise or banding in deep shadows.

CAMERA_CONTRAST.desc: Adjusts the tone curve's contrast and saturation independently of Camera Grade. 3 is stock; higher values deepen shadows and strengthen colour, with 10 targeting 170% of the firmware scales. This does not raise Camera Grade's colour-matrix or detail multipliers. Reboot to apply. High values can clip shadow detail or make colours look unnatural.

CAMERA_GRAIN.desc: Controls grain added after noise reduction. 3 is stock, 0 removes this added grain, and higher values create an increasingly visible film texture; 10 targets 16× the shipped amount. ASB patches every addNoiseWeight* key present in the device's own tuning, including mode-specific variants. High values can look coarse in shadows. Reboot to apply.

CAMERA_PORTRAIT.desc: Adjusts neural face and skin blending in supported portrait modes. Stock firmware may ship these weights at zero; higher levels can restore texture reduced by denoising, but can also make skin look artificial. Level 6 reaches the implemented blend-weight ceiling. Start at 1–2. This does not affect every camera mode. Reboot to apply.

CAMERA_LOWLIGHT.desc: Controls separate sharpening scales for macro and low-light processing. 0 follows Camera Grade; higher values add a progressively stronger correction, with 10 targeting 3.2× before firmware limits. Close subjects and high ISO can make halos more visible. Raise this only when those modes are genuinely soft. Reboot to apply.

camera_hold_enable.desc: While the camera is actively streaming, the governor keeps the current CPU ceiling and cores instead of lowering them. This can reduce performance dips during bursts or video, but uses more power while the camera remains open. On preserves the hold; Off lets normal governor rules apply. Thermal and vendor safety limits remain authoritative.

UX_MANAGE_TIMEOUTS.desc: Master switch for profile-managed interface timing. Performance shortens animations and long-press/multi-tap windows; Battery keeps stock timing. Off leaves these values under ROM control. Use Animation Speed below for a fixed animation scale independent of the power profile.

anim_speed.desc: Sets a fixed Android animation scale. −1 lets the power profile manage animations; 0 is the Android default, negative values are faster, positive values are slower, and the far-left setting disables animations. It applies to subsequent transitions. Very short or disabled animations can make transitions harder to follow but do not increase an app's actual processing speed.

UX_ANIM_FORCE_RESTART.desc: Fallback for ROMs that ignore live animation-scale changes. When enabled, a manual profile switch also restarts SystemUI: the screen may blink, the lock screen may return, and overlays from other modules can be torn down. It does not run on every automatic profile change. Leave this off unless you have confirmed that ordinary scale changes do not apply.

disable_blur.desc: Disables system window blur in areas such as the shade, notifications, volume panel and transitions. This can reduce GPU work, but replaces translucent backgrounds with solid ones; heads-up notification text may be harder to read over some content. The setting is global rather than per panel. Window blur changes live; compositor blur may require a reboot.

net_congestion_mobile.desc: Selects the TCP congestion-control algorithm for mobile data only. As Global follows the general Download Ramp card. Stock leaves the device value unchanged. BBR and CUBIC respond differently to loss and delay; neither is universally faster, and the better choice depends on the carrier and radio conditions. The card reports an unsupported algorithm instead of claiming it was applied.

net_qdisc.desc: Controls packet queuing on links not covered by the Wi-Fi and mobile cards, including USB/Bluetooth tethering, VPN and Ethernet. Stock preserves the device configuration. fq_codel can reduce latency under load, fq pairs with flow pacing, and cake offers more queue management at extra CPU cost. Results depend on the link; no option guarantees higher throughput or stutter-free video.

wifi_country.desc: Selects the Wi-Fi regulatory domain, which controls the channels and transmit rules the driver may use. Stock keeps the value supplied by the device. CR explicitly selects the Costa Rica domain; it is not a universal speed setting, and availability still depends on the ROM, access point and hardware. Use only channels and power levels permitted in your actual location.

doze_trim_whitelist.desc: Controls Android's Doze exemptions separately from Doze timing. Trimming exemptions lets user-installed apps follow idle restrictions; protected system apps such as the dialer, SMS, clock and root manager are not removed. The app list lets you keep selected messengers, mail or VPN apps exempt. Changes are recorded and restored at level 0 or on uninstall. Trimming can delay notifications and background sync.

wakelock_action.desc: Chooses whether ASB acts on persistent app wakelocks; measurement and reporting remain available either way. When enabled, only eligible user-installed apps are considered after 45+ minutes of screen-off wakefulness with evidence that the phone is staying awake. In detail: only an app that held the CPU for 10+ minutes (or holds a long lock right now) and that Android does not count as used today can be moved to Android's restricted standby bucket. Kernel/system sources, critical apps, battery-optimization exemptions, mail, navigation and keyboards are excluded. Nothing is force-stopped; restrictions can delay background work or notifications. Leave Off to inspect reports without intervention.

wakelock_fitness.desc: By default, fitness and step-counter apps are protected from ASB wakelock intervention. Limit asks Android to ignore their wakelocks so they cannot keep the CPU awake by themselves. Watch and band companion apps are excluded. Step timelines, background workouts and sync can become incomplete even if hardware step counting continues. Protect or uninstall restores the recorded state. This setting works independently of Act on Wakelocks.

night_quiet_enable.desc: During a long screen-off stretch in the learned night window, the governor pauses its own nonessential periodic work so the device can remain idle. It does not silence apps, disable radios or guarantee a specific battery saving. Off keeps normal governor scheduling around the clock. Turn it off only if you need those governor updates during the night window.

sustained_temp_enter.desc: Sets the CPU-zone temperature at which ASB begins limiting sustained performance in Manual mode. Lower values intervene earlier; higher values allow more heat before ASB backs off. The vendor's thermal limits remain active, and this slider is not a safety control. The default is 65 and the lower bound is 52 because some CPU zones read much hotter than the battery or shell. A threshold near or below the device's normal reading can cause constant throttling, longer work and more heat.

perf_ceiling_pct.desc: Caps the peak CPU and GPU performance available to ASB as a percentage of the device maximum. It mainly limits demanding work; light tasks may never reach the cap. Lower values can reduce peaks and heat but can also lengthen tasks and keep components awake longer, so battery life does not automatically improve. 100 leaves ASB without this additional cap. Start near 85 if needed and compare heat, responsiveness and drain on your device.

cool_gaming.desc: Uses an earlier thermal response during games, around 40 °C, instead of waiting for higher sustained-load thresholds. This can reduce heat, but frame rate and frame-time stability may also fall depending on the game and device. Off leaves games under the normal profile and thermal policy; it does not disable vendor thermal protection.

ltpo_video.desc: During eligible video playback, limits the panel peak to the lowest reported mode that matches 30 or 60 fps content, such as 60 Hz for either rate. ASB acts only with the screen on, audio playing, a compatible video layer, no high-smoothness request and no touch for three seconds. Touch, playback end or screen-off restores the previous value; the first instant after touch can still use the lower rate. Other frame rates are left unchanged. Matching modes avoids unnecessary refreshes without changing the video's frame rate.

smart_lab.name: Smart Lab
smart_lab.desc: Smart tries more settings for itself, one at a time and side by side with the best one so far, and keeps a setting only when the battery measured it cheaper without the cores at their ceiling more often, more janky frames or faster warming. It tests "5G Only When Needed" against 5G allowed (only when that switch is on), the unlock lift against 15 points less, and its own lean for the three apps that cost the most with the screen on. A best setting whose cost climbs by 15 % is tested again at once. Smart profile only; results appear under What Smart learned.

smart_lab_mem.name: Smart Lab: Memory Bus
smart_lab_mem.desc: Lets the lab also cap the CPU's votes on the memory bus: 75 % or 55 % of the bus maximum while the screen is calm (no touch for 10 seconds, nothing heavy, no camera), 50 % or the lowest step on quiet deep idle. Only the voters this kernel exposes are used; display, GPU, video and modem votes are never touched. Every write is read back and given back, and a value another component changed is left to it. A cap stays only if it measured cheaper.

profile_class_auto.name: Profiles by Kind of Use
profile_class_auto.desc: Performance holds the CPU ceilings at 80 % of the maximum while a light app (messenger, settings, reader) runs at ordinary load; Battery lifts them to at least 70 % while a game runs, where its own are lower. App launches, heavy work, the camera, the unlock lift, a thermal cap and the cooldown are untouched.

smart_records_balanced.name: Balanced Uses Smart's Findings
smart_records_balanced.desc: With the screen off on quiet deep idle, Balanced applies the screen-off CPU ceiling setting Smart measured as cheaper on this phone and kept through its check, when it is below Balanced's own. Nothing is tried or measured under Balanced; the ceilings are given back on wake and never raised.

ltpo_peak_force.name: Panel Maximum on Touch
ltpo_peak_force.desc: Works with Force LTPO Refresh. While the screen is being touched, SurfaceFlinger is asked for the highest mode the panel itself reports, past a ROM that keeps ordinary apps at 120 Hz. The ceiling is whatever the panel advertises - 165 Hz on the OnePlus 15; a rate the panel does not list in its mode table cannot be selected, so ASB never invents one. To make that top mode actually reachable, ASB also unlocks OnePlus's own extreme-refresh availability toggles; it never forces the panel high all the time, so the request is still released the moment the touch watcher goes idle and the panel's own frame drop comes back. The unlocked toggles and the refresh range are recorded and restored on Off or uninstall. Costs more power while you touch the screen. A ROM that refuses the request, or has no such toggles, is left alone and the badge says so.

mglru_mode.name: MGLRU Mode
mglru_mode.desc: Controls the standard MGLRU enabled bitmask only when the running kernel exposes it writable. Off requests 0, On requests 7, and Smart alone lets the Smart engine request 5 or 7 by load. Stock and uninstall restore the value captured before ASB first wrote it. Hex readback is compared numerically; a clamped value is reported as a mismatch, not success.

kernel_timer_migration.name: Timer Migration
kernel_timer_migration.desc: Controls /proc/sys/kernel/timer_migration through one bounded owner. Off requests 0 and preserves the previous ASB default; On requests 1. Stock and uninstall restore the captured pre-ASB value. The running kernel may not expose or permit the node; readback failure is shown instead of an applied claim.

kernel_sched_nr_migrate.name: Scheduler Migration Batch
kernel_sched_nr_migrate.desc: Bounds how many tasks the scheduler moves in one migration pass through the standard sched_nr_migrate node. Default 4 preserves the former balanced value; lower is not automatically better and higher is not automatically faster. Stock and uninstall restore the captured pre-ASB integer. Missing, read-only and mismatched nodes are reported honestly.

kernel_sched_autogroup.name: Scheduler Autogroup
kernel_sched_autogroup.desc: Controls sched_autogroup_enabled only when writable. On enables automatic task grouping; Off disables it. This can change responsiveness and background tasks without guaranteeing performance or battery gains. Stock and uninstall restore the pre-ASB 0/1.

kernel_sched_child_runs_first.name: Child Task Runs First
kernel_sched_child_runs_first.desc: Controls sched_child_runs_first only when writable. On runs a newly forked child before its parent; Off selects the opposite policy. This can affect latency and process startup, but is not a universal improvement. Stock and uninstall restore the pre-ASB 0/1.

descOpt.off: Do not request the child to run first.
descOpt.on: Run the child before its parent.

prof_performance_desc: Top clocks for games and heavy apps
lvi_cpu: Temperature of the CPU cores. ASB steers by one core sensor that it checks against its neighbours, so a stuck zone is never trusted; in Stock it is the hottest core. Up to about 45 °C is cool, short spikes when an app opens are normal, and throttling starts around 60 °C held for a while.
lvi_skin: Temperature of the shell - what your hand feels. It moves slowly and trails the CPU by minutes. Up to about 38 °C feels neutral, above about 42 °C the phone feels warm, and around 45 °C the system starts holding performance back.
lvi_board: Temperature of the main board under the shell. It sits between the CPU and the shell and shows heat soaking into the phone: after a game or a long charge it stays high even when the CPU has already cooled.
lvi_fsm: What ASB thinks the phone is doing: DEEP_IDLE - asleep with the screen off, LIGHT_IDLE - screen on with nothing to do, MODERATE - ordinary use, HEAVY - an app launch or a heavy page, SUSTAINED - long heavy work with heat, GAMING - a game. Each state has its own frequency ceilings.
lvi_gpu: How busy the graphics processor is, as a share of time. Scrolling and video sit around 5-30%, games at 50-100%. A game state is entered only when the load stays high, not on a single spike.
lvi_headroom: How much of the CPU hardware maximum the current ceilings allow, on the most limited cluster. 100% means nothing holds the CPU back. A low figure on a cool phone is a profile or vendor limit, not heat.
lvi_capsrc: Who set the CPU frequency ceiling right now: “ASB” - the profile and Smart; “Vendor” - the OnePlus thermal or performance service; “Thermal” - a thermal overlay; “Shell” - the profile script, for a few seconds after a switch until the governor takes over again. When the vendor holds a lower ceiling ASB leaves it alone rather than fighting it.
lvi_clamps: How often the vendor service pushed the ceiling below what ASB asked for: in the last hour, and since ASB started. A few an hour is normal; dozens mean a hot phone or an aggressive vendor mode.
lvi_learner: How many stretches of use (“{ses}” on the tile) Smart has learned from, across all twelve slots. Every 20 minutes of use and every night adds one. The more there are, the more Smart decides from measurements of your phone instead of defaults.
lvi_slot: Smart splits the day into six parts - {dp0} 0–6, {dp1} 6–9, {dp2} 9–12, {dp3} 12–17, {dp4} 17–21, {dp5} 21–24 - kept apart for weekdays (“{wd}”) and weekends (“{we}”): twelve slots, each with its own measurements. This is the slot the phone is in now. What a workday morning costs is not spent on a Sunday morning.
lvi_conf: How much Smart trusts what it has measured for this slot. The figure grows with every stretch of use; while it is low, Smart leans on neighbouring slots and safe defaults instead of guessing from a handful of samples.
lvi_alpha: How far the current policy leans from {bal} toward {bat}, in percent, learned from what this slot usually costs. 0% is {bal} behaviour; higher values hold the phone back more to save charge. Heat, a game or a camera session pushes it back down on its own.
lvi_apphint: What the foreground load looks like right now: “{app0}”, “{app1}”, “{app2}”, “{app3}” or “{app4}”. Smart reads it from the app in front and the load it creates, and gives games and heavy work more frequency headroom than a messenger.
lvi_basis: What steers Smart right now. Usually the records for the situation you are in: “{rec}” - a setting cheaper than the original one by the share shown was found, checked by pairs of measurements; “{rok}” - the original setting is already the best; “{trial}” - a neighbouring setting is being tried, pairs done of pairs needed. “{smt}” / “{smo}” - this app’s smoothness is being tested, or the extra headroom that helped it is kept. While this time slot has little history, the tile shows where Smart borrows from: “{fb1}”, “{fb2}”, “{fb3}”, “{fb4}”. Protection comes first: “{cold}”, “{lowb}”, “{brief}”, “{night}”, “{guard}”. Below: the records of every situation.
lvi_slotheat: Not the temperature now - how warm this slot usually runs. Smart remembers the CPU peak of every stretch of use in each slot and compares this slot with the phone’s own norm, the middle of all its slots: “{hcool}”, “{hnorm}” or “{hwarm}”. A slot that usually runs warm gets slightly gentler ceilings in advance, before the phone heats up; one that runs cool gets a little headroom back.
lvi_trend: Where the phone’s temperature is heading: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. A warming trend makes Smart back off before a hard thermal limit is reached; cooling gives the headroom back. Right after a profile switch the trend stays muted for two minutes, so a stale reading cannot steer the new profile.
lvi_lpm: The modem’s power mode, read from the governor’s own state file: “{lnormal}” follows the profile; “{lsave}” lets the radio idle with stretched keepalives (screen off or the {bat} profile); “{lfast}” keeps latency low for games and downloads; “{lnight}” stretches idling further inside the night window Smart learned from your routine.
lvi_cpuceil: How much of the hardware maximum the ROM lets the CPU reach right now, on the most limited cluster. In Stock ASB sets no ceilings, so anything under 100% here comes from the OnePlus thermal or performance service.
lvi_gpuclk: The graphics clock at this moment. It drops to the minimum when nothing is drawn and climbs with load; in Stock ASB does not touch it.
lvi_battemp: Battery temperature. Above about 40 °C charging slows down and the battery ages faster; above about 45 °C the system limits performance to protect it.
lvi_zram: Compressed memory (zRAM) in use. Android packs apps you have not used for a while here instead of closing them. Several GB is normal with many apps open; it costs CPU time only when an app is unpacked again.
lvi_learnpause: In Stock Smart neither learns nor decides - the ASB frequency policy is off. Everything it has learned is kept and is used again as soon as you switch back to Smart.
eta_meter_tip: Estimate: nothing measured since the governor started - based on the screen-on drain ASB measured earlier in this profile, over %s min.
lvi_sdrain: The current flowing out of the battery right now, read straight from the battery driver. It jumps with every tap and falls when the screen goes off - the hourly drain with the screen on and off is in the two tiles above. Below: this current as an hourly rate.
lvi_strend: Where the CPU temperature is heading, from ROM readings every 10 seconds over the last two minutes: “{up}”, “{fl}” or “{dn}”. In {stock} nothing in ASB reacts to it; it shows what the phone’s own thermal management is working against. For the first half-minute after Monitor opens it is still measuring (…).
lvi_slpm: Whether the ROM keeps mobile data up while Wi-Fi is connected (the “mobile data always active” developer setting): “{lfast}” - kept up, a faster handover for a little more drain; “{lnormal}” - the ROM’s default. In {stock} ASB applies no modem policy; this is the ROM’s own setting.
lvi_sram: Memory available to apps right now without closing anything, next to the phone’s total. Android keeps apps in memory on purpose, so a low figure is not a problem unless apps keep restarting.
lvi_sclock: The highest current clock among the CPU clusters in this reading. It changes many times a second, so one reading says little on its own; below, the clock of every cluster.
lvi_sload: System load over the last minute: how many tasks were running or waiting - for the CPU or for storage - on average. Android counts storage waits too, so this number alone can read past the core count on a phone that is doing almost nothing; that is normal, not an overload. The percentage beside it is the part of the last seconds the cores were genuinely busy, measured from /proc/stat between two readings. The 5- and 15-minute figures and the per-core share are in the tooltip.
lvi_sbattery: Charge level and voltage, read straight from the battery driver. The voltage falls as the charge goes down and sags briefly under load; below, the battery temperature.
lvi_suptime: Time since the phone was last started. Below: when that was, and how long the screen was on and off since then.
lvi_trend_rate: %1 °C per minute over the last %2 s

nf_card_desc: Notifications from some apps arrive late? Choose those apps: ASB exempts them from sleep and background limits and shows what else holds push back.
nf_copy: Tick the apps whose notifications arrive late - only after you open the app, or only when the screen turns on - then tap Fix. ASB exempts them from Doze and background limits, lifts background-data blocks for them, keeps its own sleep and wakelock policies off them and checks what else delays push. The previous state is recorded and comes back when you untick an app.
nf_oem_note: On OxygenOS also check “Allow background activity” and auto-launch in the app’s own settings - the ROM keeps those itself and ASB does not change them.

nf_f_wakelock: ASB restricts apps that hold the phone awake at night: the chosen apps are excluded automatically.
nf_f_heytap: HeyTap/OPPO push is off: apps that deliver through it get no push at all.
nf_f_athena: The ROM’s own background killer (Athena) is active: it can close messengers in the background and no exemption above stops it. Switching it off keeps apps alive at a cost of RAM and some battery.

This can improve startup, but does not guarantee battery savings; compilation itself costs CPU and storage writes.

lr_impact_cap_fmt: {yes}% at cap vs {no}% below cap · {frames} frames

zy_mode_battery_desc: Observer and process journal, plus the evidence-gated background guard. Cold-start lifts and lifecycle requests are off. Approved restrictions can delay background work and notifications.
zy_mode_performance_desc: Observer, process journal and cold-start assistance. Background guard is off. Existing profile and thermal gates still apply; a faster device is not guaranteed.
zy_mode_auto_desc: Cold-start assistance and lifecycle hints for responsiveness, plus the evidence-gated background guard. ART stays separate. This balances mechanisms; it does not promise maximum speed and battery life at once.
zy_mode_custom_unified: Custom: switches or the guard differ from the preset. ASB will not silently undo your manual choice. Choose a mode above to reapply its complete set.
zy_mode_custom_warning: Manual override active. In particular, cold-start or lifecycle requests added to Battery can increase activity; the interface will not keep calling that set Battery.
zy_auto_managed_by_mode: Follows the mode above · no package lists to fill in
zy_auto_desc_unified: The selected mode automatically fills the observation list with user apps and applies its matching switches and guard baseline. ART compilation remains a separate manual choice below.
zy_settings_custom: Manual override active; ASB will not silently restore a preset.
zy_controls_note: These switches fine-tune the current mode. A mismatch is shown as Custom and is never silently rolled back. Master, cold-start and ledger changes affect newly started or restarted app processes.
zy_control_failed: Zygisk setting was not changed; check the current state
zy_off_desc: ASB will not attach to Zygisk in newly started app processes. Apps that are already running keep their previous state until they are restarted.
zy_off_kept: Your mode, automatic app selection, feature switches, guard and ART settings are preserved. Enabling again restores that setup; it does not silently choose a new preset.
lr_detail_cpu_peak: The highest sampled CPU thermal reading in this capture, not the average temperature and not proof of sustained throttling. The duration above 45 °C and the named hottest phase below show how long and where heat actually persisted.
lr_detail_drain: Battery percentage lost divided by eligible off-charger time. Charging is excluded. The estimate from a full charge is only this capture’s pace projected forward, not a promise of battery life or proof that a tweak caused the result.
lr_detail_idle: This is the longest eligible quiet screen-off chain, not the average of every short pause and not necessarily a whole night. Deep sleep is the share when the device was not awake. Short chains and whole-percent battery steps can make the rate noisy.
lr_detail_idle_floor: A stable verdict needs an idle chain of at least two hours.
lr_detail_jank: The share of sampled frames that missed their deadline. It describes rendered frames in this capture; it does not by itself identify whether the app, ROM, thermal state or ASB caused the delay. Use the per-app and wake-window breakdown below.
lr_detail_jps: Janky frames divided by sampled frame time. Unlike a percentage, this also reflects how often a visible hitch occurred. It is an observed smoothness metric, not an FPS average or proof that changing a ceiling will improve it.
lr_detail_skin_peak: The highest sampled surface or skin-sensor reading. It is closer to how warm the phone feels than the CPU die peak, but it is still a snapshot maximum. The time above 40 °C below is the useful duration evidence.
lr_zy_detail_events: Accepted start/exit notifications from the observer lifecycle channel. This is not a count of boosted apps and does not measure a performance gain.
lr_zy_detail_hints: Lifecycle hints ask the governor to refresh its policy after a relevant app state change. Zero means that no hint was sent in this interval, not that apps had no lifecycle events. Accepted or vetoed describes the request only; it is not an energy measurement.
lr_zy_detail_ipc: CPU time spent by the observer IPC path between the two snapshots. It covers this observer path, not every ASB component. Milliseconds per wakeup are shown only when both counters are known; neither number proves a net battery cost or saving.
wl_service_confirm: Disable only %s? The app package is not frozen, but this service can stop working until restored. Notifications, sync, media, calls, alarms or other app features may break. ASB records and restores the exact original component state.
wl_service_copy: Disable one Android service component, not the whole app. This is component disabling, not a process freezer. The list comes from currently running service records; it does not prove that a service holds a wakelock or costs energy. Restore returns the recorded default/enabled state.
wl_service_empty: No running service components are exposed for this app right now. This does not prove that the app has no services; start or use the app, then refresh. Components already disabled through ASB remain listed for Restore.
wl_service_external: Already disabled outside ASB; it was not adopted and will not be restored by ASB
wl_service_loading: Reading running services and actual component states…
wl_service_meta: %s service(s) selected · on-demand read · no automatic freezing or polling
wl_service_not_running: The service is no longer running or its original state is not exposed; nothing was changed
wl_service_state_lapsed: Selected, but not disabled now · use Restore to finish restoring it
wl_service_state_running: Running now · the app package remains enabled
wl_service_state_unknown: Current component state is not exposed
wl_service_unavailable: Service records or component state are not exposed right now. Nothing was changed.
lr_sm_state_adapting: Smart active · {n} log hints accepted in this capture
lr_sm_state_active: Smart active · native A/B owns decisions
lr_sm_state_manual: Manual profile at the last snapshot · stored records are not live adaptation
lr_sm_state_disabled: Smart profile, but Smart mode is off
lr_sm_feedback_note: The log supplies sustained-jank evidence only. Smart re-reads Android frame statistics and owns A/B windows, plateau and cooldown decisions; report recommendations are never executed as settings.
lr_sum_drain_mixed_segments: Average drain across {segments} off-charger windows over {h}, screen on {on}% of the capture: about {est} from a full charge at this pace.
lr_brief_drain_segments: Off the charger, total consumption was {drop}% over {h} across {segments} windows - {pct}%/h on average. This is a sum across windows, not one charge. Latest window: {lastdrop}% over {lasth} ({lastpct}%/h). At this average pace, a full charge would last about {est}.
lr_brief_drain_segments_short: Off the charger, total consumption was {drop}% over {h} across {segments} windows ({pct}%/h). This is a sum across windows, not one charge. Latest window: {lastdrop}% over {lasth} ({lastpct}%/h).
lr_drain_sum_windows: Sum across {n} off-charger windows: −{drop}% (not one charge)
lr_detail_drain_windows: The total is a sum of separate windows between charging sessions, so it can exceed 100%. It is not the drop of one battery charge.
zy_aot_exclude_hint: If an app misbehaves after compilation, exclude it: ASB will never compile it again and, if ASB compiled it, returns it to the compile state Android installed it with.
zy_aot_excluded_title: Excluded by you (%s): ASB does not compile these apps.
zy_aot_included: ASB may compile this app again
zy_aot_excluded_reset: Excluded · its compile state is being returned to how Android installed it
zy_aot_excluded_done: Excluded · ASB will not compile this app
lr_dx_smooth_wake_external: Stutter concentrates at unlocks and app opens: {pct}% of frames late there against {ord}% over the day. The firmware held the prime cores below ASB's ceiling in {n} of {of} checks, so ASB's touch boost cannot lift them; this capture does not show that ASB caused these late frames.
lsp_ab_a: A/B test of %m: day with the module, %h h so far. It needs 24 h with at least 6 h of screen-off and 1 h of screen-on.
lsp_ab_b_wait: A/B test of %m: the first day is measured and the module is switched off. Reboot to start the day without it.
lsp_ab_b: A/B test of %m: day without the module, %h h so far.
lsp_ab_done_worse: A/B test of %m: without it the phone used measurably less. The module is switched back on (after a reboot); consider lightening it.
lsp_ab_done_neutral: A/B test of %m: no measurable difference between the two days. The module is switched back on (after a reboot).
lsp_ab_aborted: A/B test of %m stopped: %r. The module is switched back on (after a reboot).
lsp_ab_r_coverage: not enough screen-off and screen-on time within 4 days
lsp_ab_cpu: CPU of its apps, with → without
lsp_ab_profile: The profile changed between the two days, so the comparison is weaker.
lsp_ab_honest: Two different days: usage, signal and temperature differ too. A difference counts only above 15 % and a fixed floor.
lsp_unread: The LSPosed state has not been read yet.
lsp_db: LSPosed's database could not be read (%s); nothing is changed.
lsp_desc: Which modules are on, what they hook and what that costs: from LSPosed's own database, Android's usage history, the Zygisk start ledger and crash records that pass through a module. LSPosed reports no energy per hook, so a verdict is a reasoned estimate; the A/B test measures one module directly.
lsp_refreshing: Reading the evidence in the background…
lsp_no_evidence: No evidence read yet: verdicts use the scopes only.
lsp_no_usage: Android's usage history could not be read, so unused apps are not detected.
lsp_pending: Changes are written to LSPosed and take effect after a reboot.
lsp_auto_desc: Once a day ASB removes a module's scope from apps you have not opened for %d days that still start in the background, and from apps its hooks keep crashing. Messengers, mail, authenticators, wearables, alarms, navigation, your Doze keep list and notification-fixed apps are never touched, and no module is switched off. Every change is listed below with Undo.
lsp_manual_desc: Nothing changes until you confirm it. Lighten removes a module's scope only from apps listed under it; the framework, SystemUI and the module itself are never touched.
lsp_c_unused: %a: not opened for %d days, %b background starts/day
lsp_t_busy: This module is in an A/B test
lsp_t_done: Done · takes effect after a reboot
lsp_r_bgheavy: its apps start often in the background
lsp_r_unused: hooks apps you do not open
lsp_r_ab_worse: A/B test: it costs battery or CPU
lsp_age_fresh: Evidence read less than an hour ago.
s7_budget_desc: A rarely opened app that keeps starting in the background goes to Android's "rare" standby bucket; opening it brings it back. Automatic: unused 7+ days and 6+ background starts a day; on the Battery profile also without this switch, at 14+ days and 10+ starts. Messengers, mail, 2FA, wearables, alarms, navigation, keyboards, launchers, system apps and your Doze keep list are never touched.
s7_data_desc: An app you have not opened for 3+ days that still moves mobile data in the background loses background data on metered networks (Android's own per-app switch). Automatic from 10 MB a day; Wi-Fi and the app in use are not affected.
s7_charge: Charge end learned from your mornings
s7_charge_desc: With the night charge limit on, the hold ends 90 minutes before the time you usually unplug (median of the last 4 weeks, weekdays and weekends apart), so the phone is full when you take it.
s7_no_evidence: No usage data read yet; candidates appear after a refresh.
s7_need: Budgets need Android's usage history and the Zygisk start ledger; data needs network statistics.
s7_mb: %s MB/day mobile data in the background
lvr_confirming: check: %1 once more against %2, which it beat, %3 of %4 pairs
s7l_none: Nothing learned yet: the figures appear after some use off the charger.
s7l_apps_note: Battery current × voltage while the app was in front, the screen included; fades by 3 % a day.
s7l_budget_lean: At the current drain the battery will not last until then: Smart leans to economy.
s7l_budget_relax: The battery lasts until then with room to spare: no low-battery lean.
s7l_conf_checking: checking the new best setting once more
s7l_class_perf: Performance: light app held at 80 % of the CPU maximum
s7l_class_bat: Battery: game lifted to 70 % of the CPU maximum
s7l_replay: Balanced: the screen-off setting Smart won is in use
s7l_lsp: Smoothness tests skipped in apps hooked by a costly LSPosed module: %s
s7l_ddr: Memory bus on quiet screen-off: at its lowest step in %1 % of the governor's reads, average %2 MHz (lowest %3 MHz). Each read is taken at the governor's own wake, so this is an upper bound.
s7l_wait_gauge: The cost per app waits for the battery gauge check: ASB first compares the current reading with the real drain over a few screen-on stretches.
t_cfg_needs_ltpo: · works once Force LTPO Refresh is on
nc_state_holding_switch: charging paused at 80% (charge switch, not a charge limit)
s7_external: already changed by another component - left as it is
s7l_lab: Smart lab: settings tried side by side
s7l_lab_off_radio: waits for the "5G Only When Needed" switch
s7l_lab_off_mem: no memory-bus voter this kernel lets ASB write
s7l_lab_reopen: · tested again after its cost rose (%s×)
s7l_lab_mem: Memory bus: %1 voter(s) found (%2), cap now %3
s7l_lab_none: No experiment has finished a block yet: each needs several pairs of blocks off the charger.
s7l_lab_note: A setting wins only when the battery measured it at least 3 % cheaper, side by side, without the cores at their ceiling more often, more janky frames or faster warming.
cfg_inf_section_battery_hint: Recompiles apps, then resets Android’s stored battery statistics at the next reboot. Offered only at a full charge.
cfg_inf_section_repairs_hint: One-tap, reversible repairs for specific OxygenOS/ColorOS problems.
bfx_desc: Two steps. First every app is recompiled in place (speed-profile), with progress shown below app by app. Then, on the next reboot, Android’s stored battery statistics are reset, so the per-app usage history and the learned capacity estimate start again from a full charge. This clears a skewed record; it does not add capacity or battery life. Available only at 100% on charge.
bfx_confirm: Tap again to run Battery Fix
bfx_refused: Not available right now — needs 100% on charge
inf_hero_sub: One-time repairs for specific problems. Each one shows its progress and what it changed.
bfx_art_failed: Could not read the list of apps
bfx_reset_pending: Scheduled — applied at the next reboot
bfx_reset_fresh: Android has started a new record
bfx_reset_wait: Android will write the new record by itself shortly
bfx_stopping: Recompiling stops after the current app
bfx_started: Started: apps are being recompiled; the statistics reset follows the reboot
cfg_kernel_section_controls_hint: Only registered writable interfaces are controlled here. Availability and live readback come from the running kernel.
cfg_kernel_section_wakeup_hint: An optional exact-name list for a kernel with the ASB wakeup interface. Empty by default.
kernel_wb_sub: Up to 16 names, 1–63 printable ASCII characters each. No spaces, paths, patterns or automatic rules.
kernel_wb_warning: Only add a name after diagnosing a concrete wakeup source. Blocking can delay notifications, networking or sensors. Existing locks are not force-released.
kernel_wb_empty: No rules — nothing is blocked by ASB.
kernel_wb_diff: Saved policy and kernel readback differ. Apply the policy or refresh after another owner changes it.
kernel_wb_invalid: Use one exact printable ASCII name without spaces, slashes or backslashes
kernel_wb_duplicate: This name is already in the list
kernel_wb_limit: The kernel accepts at most 16 rules
kernel_wb_policy_error: Policy could not be saved atomically
cfg_inf_section_cleanup_hint: Manual removal of diagnostic residue and files already placed in a trash state.
junk_desc: Removes crash reports, ANR traces, diagnostic and installer caches, stale backup journals and files already in a trash state. Ordinary screenshots, recent tasks, module settings and working files are preserved. This frees storage; it does not prove or guarantee a fix for lag.
junk_confirm: Tap again to delete the listed files permanently, including trashed screenshots
junk_failed: Could not scan the supported locations
junk_partial: Not everything was removed; failed categories: {count}
kernel_controls_help: Each switch below writes only its named standard kernel interface. Stock restores the value captured before ASB first wrote it. Missing or read-only interfaces are disabled; a different readback is reported as a mismatch, not as success.
